disposition_reason: Table 1 prints lead in 48 jarred wild boar ragù samples (16 brands x 3 batches) with brand means; the text gives medians by meat share and processing region.

study.design: market survey of ready-to-eat jarred wild boar ragù, three batches of each of 16 brands
study.origin: wild boar meat processed in three establishments in Emilia-Romagna, Toscana and Trentino Alto-Adige, Italy
study.market: Italian food stores and online distribution
study.method: HNO3 digestion (Digi-Prep, 75 C overnight) of two 3 g subsamples; ICP-MS (Agilent 7700)
study.qa: validated per Reg. 333/2007/EU; recovery >80%; BCR-185R bovine liver in every batch; FAPAS and EURL proficiency tests; uncertainty 20-22%

controls.control: proportion of wild boar meat in the ragù
controls.outcome: median Pb 0.07, 0.10 and 0.16 mg/kg; no significant correlation between meat percentage and Pb (r = -0.18, p = 0.21)

controls.comparator: Emilia-Romagna vs Toscana vs Trentino Alto-Adige
controls.outcome: median Pb 0.05, 0.15 and 0.09 mg/kg; no significant difference
brand means 0.02 to 6.16 mg/kg; no significant difference among brands; high values driven by single batches (e.g. 18.3, 9.00, 5.80 mg/kg)

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU maximum level for lead in meat of cattle, pig, lamb and chicken (no game-meat ML)

unresolved: Table 1 prints one value per batch; whether it is the mean of the two subsamples is not stated.
Source of lead (ammunition fragments) is inferred by the authors, not measured.
